world.title: West Asia war LIVE: China, Pakistan call on U.S. and Iran to resume talks
world.summary: China and Pakistan have urged the U.S. and Iran to resume diplomatic talks amid escalating tensions in West Asia. Recent U.S. airstrikes targeted Iranian positions on Qeshm Island and near Bandar Abbas, impacting shipping activity. On July 16, only three vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz, the lowest daily count since May, following Iranian attacks on maritime targets.

world.title: US-Iran news LIVE: Sirens go off in Qatar after US targets Iranian bridges; White House says Tehran still wants deal
world.summary: Sirens were activated in Qatar following US airstrikes targeting Iranian bridges and a railway station, as reported by Fars News Agency. Additionally, power lines in Bandar Abbas and nearby villages suffered damage. In response, Iran launched attacks on American bases in the Gulf region. The White House stated that Tehran remains interested in pursuing a deal.

world.title: Trump says US 'winning big' in Iran, cites Venezuela as blueprint for strategy: 'Will see fruits very shortly'
world.summary: US President Donald Trump stated that the US is "winning big" in Iran, drawing parallels to its strategy in Venezuela. He claimed Venezuela is collaborating with the US to produce millions of barrels of oil. Trump's comments come amid escalating tensions in the US-Iran conflict, suggesting that positive outcomes from these strategies will be seen "very shortly."

business.title: JPMorgan says 100+ MNCs are exploring GIFT City operations
business.summary: JPMorgan reports that over 100 multinational companies are considering operations in GIFT City, attracted by its banking and payment solutions for corporate treasury functions. The city offers tax incentives, a single regulatory framework, and foreign currency capabilities, enhancing its appeal. These factors are positioning GIFT City as a potential global financial hub for multinational treasury centers in India.

business.title: New Toyota Hilux Teased Ahead Of India Launch On 28th July
business.summary: Toyota is set to launch the new 9th-generation Hilux in India on July 28. While the global model features mild-hybrid and battery electric vehicle (BEV) options, the India-specific version is anticipated to maintain the current 2.8-litre turbo diesel engine. The company is preparing for the introduction of this updated model in the Indian market.

business.title: Govt weighs lower than 0.5% MDR on UPI transactions for large merchants
business.summary: The government is contemplating a merchant discount rate (MDR) for UPI transactions involving large merchants, potentially set below 0.5 percent. This fee would be applicable solely to merchants and not to consumers. The move aims to regulate transaction costs for larger businesses utilizing the Unified Payments Interface, although specific details and implementation timelines remain under discussion.

technology.title: Apple iPhone 18 Pro Max: Will it cross Rs 1.50 lakh in India? Reports reveal expected price
technology.summary: Reports suggest that the Apple iPhone 18 Pro Max may exceed Rs 1.50 lakh in India. Counterpoint Research estimates the bill of materials (BOM) for the 1TB variant at approximately USD 900, which is USD 350 higher than the iPhone 17 Pro Max’s estimated BOM of USD 550. Pricing details remain speculative as the launch approaches.

technology.title: EU orders Google to share search data with rivals, broaden Android feature access
technology.summary: The European Union has mandated Google LLC to modify its business practices in search and mobile markets. This directive includes sharing search data with competitors and expanding access to Android features. The changes are detailed in two binding specification measures issued by the European Commission, aimed at fostering competition and ensuring a fairer digital marketplace for all stakeholders.

technology.title: EU Commission sets binding rules for Google on Android AI interoperability and Search data sharing
technology.summary: The European Commission has introduced binding rules for Google regarding Android AI interoperability and search data sharing, as part of the Digital Markets Act. These measures aim to promote competition by ensuring that competitors' AI systems can interact effectively with Google's platforms and that data sharing practices are transparent and fair, enhancing the overall digital market landscape.

sports.title: Rohit too good a player to feel pressure: Sitanshu Kotak
sports.summary: Indian batting coach Sitanshu Kotak expressed confidence in Rohit Sharma's abilities despite his poor performance in the second ODI against England, where India lost by four wickets. Kotak emphasized that Rohit is too skilled to feel pressure and believes he will perform well in the upcoming ODI at Lord's. The series is currently tied at one match each.

sports.title: 'Nothing was handed to Argentina': Lionel Messi unloads on favouritism claims
sports.summary: Lionel Messi has responded to critics alleging favoritism in Argentina's journey to the FIFA World Cup final. He emphasized that the defending champions have rightfully earned their place through their performances, rejecting claims of favorable officiating or external influences. Messi's comments highlight the team's dedication and hard work, asserting that their success is a result of their own efforts.

sports.title: Where's the hitman? Rohit Sharma's form a growing concern for India's ODI World Cup plans
sports.summary: Rohit Sharma's performance in the ODI series against England raises concerns for India's World Cup plans. He scored only 37 runs across two matches, with a 21-ball 11 at Edgbaston and a 47-ball 26 at Sophia Gardens. His struggle to find form may impact India's strategy as they prepare for the upcoming World Cup tournament.

health.title: Beyond MBBS: Why health literacy challenge needs more than doctors
health.summary: In India, healthcare trust is increasingly shifting from doctors to online sources, underscoring a critical need for enhanced health literacy. As urban migration has distanced individuals from traditional family doctors, many now seek medical information online. This change highlights the importance of improving public understanding of health issues, ensuring that individuals can make informed decisions about their healthcare.

health.title: WHO gets less than half funding to fight Ebola in DRC
health.summary: The World Health Organization has received only 40% of the $115 million needed to combat the Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. A WHO official emphasized the urgency of the situation, urging donors to continue their support during this critical phase of the epidemic. The lack of funding poses significant challenges to effective response efforts.

health.title: Can't stop sneezing this monsoon? Doctor says it could be more than an allergy, and these warning signs should never be ignored
health.summary: During the monsoon, persistent sneezing may indicate more than seasonal allergies. While many attribute symptoms like a runny nose to allergies, they can also stem from viral infections, sinus issues, or asthma-related inflammation. Misdiagnosing these conditions can lead to ineffective treatments. It is crucial to recognize when sneezing warrants further medical attention to address the underlying cause effectively.

science.title: Could we create a black hole in a laboratory on Earth?
science.summary: Creating a black hole in a laboratory could provide valuable insights into the universe's workings. Currently, all observed black holes are natural phenomena located far from Earth. Researchers, including astronomers, are exploring the feasibility of laboratory-created black holes to study their interactions with surrounding matter. This endeavor could enhance our understanding of fundamental astrophysical processes.

science.title: How a hidden shift in the Atlantic could rewire the seasons
science.summary: A human-sized, uncrewed probe is currently drifting in the deep waters off Greenland, analyzing underwater conditions. Equipped with advanced sensors, the probe aims to gather crucial data that may reveal significant changes in the Atlantic Ocean's currents. These findings could potentially alter seasonal weather patterns, highlighting the importance of understanding ocean dynamics in relation to climate change.

science.title: An ‘Asteroid’ Tracked Since 1998 Made an Unexplained Orbital Shift-Now Astronomers Say It’s Something Far More Mysterious
science.summary: Astronomers have reported an unexplained orbital shift of a space object tracked since 1998, initially believed to be an asteroid. Last summer, during its near approach, the object did not appear where predicted, leading researchers to reconsider its classification. This unexpected behavior has prompted further investigation into the object's nature, suggesting it may be something more mysterious than previously thought.

entertainment.title: Aamir Khan says 3 Idiots wasn't inspired by Sonam Wangchuk, expresses concern over his health: ‘Hope he ends his fast’
entertainment.summary: Aamir Khan addressed rumors regarding his character Rancho in "3 Idiots," stating it was not inspired by activist Sonam Wangchuk. He expressed concern for Wangchuk's health amid his ongoing indefinite hunger strike, hoping for a resolution. Khan made these remarks during a special appearance at the London Indian Film Festival, coinciding with the screening of "Lagaan."

entertainment.title: Why Nolan’s vision for 'The Odyssey' doesn't fit on India’s screens
entertainment.summary: Only 41 theatres worldwide can project 'The Odyssey' in its original 15/70mm format, with India lacking any commercial venue for this. Consequently, Indian audiences will only see digital versions of the film. The limitations stem from architectural and economic factors affecting multiplex operators, influencing the post-production process and the ability to showcase the film as intended.

entertainment.title: 'I used full body makeup to match the colour of my face with my body': Sameera Reddy reveals on being made ‘two to three shades lighter’ in her debut film 'Maine Dil Tujhko Diya' with Sohail Khan
entertainment.summary: Sameera Reddy disclosed that during her debut film 'Maine Dil Tujhko Diya', she was made two to three shades lighter using makeup, and wore padded bras and bum pads. She also used colored lenses. Reddy, who returned to Hindi cinema after 14 years in 'Aakhri', shared her struggles with body image and skin color insecurities until her 40s.
